name: MoReBench Rubric Profile Validation
description: Rubric-set validation workflow for MoReBench. This phase treats all rubric annotations for one query as one structured profile and drops criterion-title classification as a target.
goal: Validate what can be learned from the query text about the full expert rubric profile before moving to response fulfillment and activation captures.

rubric_structure.unit: one dilemma/query with a set of expert-written rubric criteria
rubric_structure.notes: Criteria are multiple annotations for one query. Phase 1 should validate aggregate rubric-profile structure, not classify criterion titles into their own rubric labels.

research_questions: What is the rubric profile attached to each query: dominant weighted dimension, harmlessness penalties, helpful-vs-harmless tension, complexity, and high-weight focus?
Can query text alone predict the dominant weighted rubric dimension?
Can query text alone predict whether the rubric includes negative harmless-outcome penalties?
Can query text alone predict helpful-vs-harmless tension in the rubric profile?
Can query text alone predict rubric complexity?
Which profile attributes are mostly topic-readable and which require explicit rubric-set context?

workflow_steps.name: build_rubric_profiles
workflow_steps.question: Collapse all criteria for a query into one scenario-level rubric profile.
workflow_steps.interpretation: This is the central validation artifact for Phase 1. It preserves the fact that MoReBench provides multiple annotations per query.

workflow_steps.name: dilemma_text_to_dominant_dimension_baseline
workflow_steps.question: Can query text predict the dominant weighted rubric dimension for the whole rubric set?
workflow_steps.interpretation: High metrics mean rubric profile shape is topic-readable. Low metrics mean later probes need explicit rubric context.

workflow_steps.name: dilemma_text_to_harmless_penalty_baseline
workflow_steps.question: Can query text predict whether any negative harmless-outcome penalty is present?
workflow_steps.interpretation: High metrics mean safety-penalty requirements are mostly scenario-topic shortcuts. Low metrics mean the penalty comes from expert rubric structure.

workflow_steps.name: dilemma_text_to_helpful_harmless_tension_baseline
workflow_steps.question: Can query text predict whether the rubric has both helpful-outcome reward mass and harmless-outcome penalty mass?
workflow_steps.interpretation: High metrics mean helpful-vs-harmless tension is visible in the query alone. Low metrics mean the tension must be represented through the rubric set.

workflow_steps.name: dilemma_text_to_rubric_complexity_baseline
workflow_steps.question: Can query text predict whether the expert rubric is low, medium, or high complexity?
workflow_steps.interpretation: High metrics mean complexity is topic-readable. Low metrics mean complexity is additional expert structure.

next_experiments.name: response_fulfillment_labels
next_experiments.description: Generate model answers and judge criterion fulfillment per rubric item. Aggregate signed weighted scores by dimension and total score.

next_experiments.name: rubric_conditioned_capture
next_experiments.description: Capture residual activations for prompts containing the query plus the rubric set or selected criteria, without exposing profile labels. Probe profile attributes and criterion fulfillment.

next_experiments.name: helpful_harmless_tradeoff_geometry
next_experiments.description: Use profile labels and fulfillment labels to build helpful-vs-harmless directions, geometry views, and causal steering/patching tests.

controls: The validation unit is base_dilemma_id, not individual criterion title.
Do not treat criterion-title to rubric-dimension classification as a scientific result.
Use text-only query baselines as leakage checks for profile attributes before activation probes.
Keep criterion text, query text, and generated response text as separable fields.
Do not include profile labels in model prompts used for activation captures.

dataset.loader: Deferred HuggingFaceSource with nested RUBRIC expansion at runtime

capture.status: planned after rubric-profile validation and response-fulfillment label design

outputs.notes: The report should describe the rubric profile distribution and query-text predictability for each profile attribute.
